quotes.text: Data center development represents possible economic development opportunities but requires large amounts of land, of energy, and of water which impacts the communities in which they are located. Moreover, the requests are increasing quickly without consideration of needed rules and guidelines.

No Virginian should pay a dime more for energy or water because of data centers. If they cannot meet that requirement, they shouldn’t be built. [...] Data centers and tech companies must fully cover their own operational and infrastructure costs including water, electricity, and the construction of new transmission lines. [...] If a community does not want a data center, it must have the right to say no.

Data centers and monopoly utilities are getting rich off of our tax dollars. And jacking up our rates. [...] Wittman traded half a million dollars in data center stocks and gave them billions in tax breaks. [...] That’s why we need to ban congressional stock trading.

Virginia has more data centers than anybody, except for maybe Texas. The first thing is, nobody in the first congressional district should pay one dime more for energy or water that is being utilized by these data centers. They need to pay their own way. They need to start engaging in more renewable sources, like using solar panels at their locations, wind turbines, storage batteries.

I'm not using the word moratorium. Artificial intelligence has a data center component to it, but certainly for cloud storage-based companies like Google, like Microsoft, we need to start paying attention to what is happening in our areas and how our citizens feel about them.
